anomalies.observed: The WS2812B status LED D10 has its data input (DIN, pin 4) tied to net NET0014. That same label NET0014 is on ESP32-C3 U1 pin 14 (GPIO1/ADC1_CH1/XTAL_32K_N) and on both the IN and DIAG_EN pins (pins 1/2) of the heater high-side switch U11 (TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1), as well as on the heater indicator LED D8/R4 and the J7 connector. Thus the LED data line and the heater control line are one and the same net.
anomalies.expected: The WS2812B status LED must be driven by its own dedicated GPIO data line, electrically separate from the heater control net. The specification assigns the heater to GPIO1 and describes the WS2812B as an independent firmware-driven status indicator (colors for run states), which is impossible if it shares the bang-bang heater GPIO.

evidence.quote: NET0014 label attached to D10 (WS2812B) DIN pin, sheet /Microcontroller/ (mcu.kicad_sch, right-hand side)
NET0014 label on U1 pin 14 GPIO1/ADC1_CH1/XTAL_32K_N and on U11 DIAG_EN/IN pins, sheet /Microcontroller/ (mcu.kicad_sch)
Drives a single heater output net through a smart high-side switch (U6, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) switched from the ESP32's GPIO1

anomalies.impact: The status LED cannot be driven with the WS2812B serial protocol because its data line is shared with the heater on/off GPIO; conversely the heater switch input would receive WS2812B data bursts, causing spurious heater switching, and the LED would only ever show a static level.

parsed.summary: The drawing shows the WS2812B status LED's data input (D10 DIN) on the same net (NET0014) as the ESP32 GPIO1 heater-control line that drives the TPS1H200 high-side switch, which would make the status LED and the heater mutually unusable; this is the main deviation found.
